title: Counterfoil
label: A merchant-record gate for AI payments
text: An AI returns agent can ask for a refund that the store does not owe. Counterfoil checks the request against the merchant's records before it reaches Braintree. This walkthrough uses screenshots of the deployed application and recorded evidence.

title: Meet the store
label: HOMI · fictional fixtures · sandbox only
text: HOMI is our fictional homeware store. A Reader extracts fields from the customer's email. A separate Runner asks for payment tools. Counterfoil checks ownership, return entitlement, reservations, item prices and disputes. The decision is pass, hold for a person, or block.

title: Same request. Three checks.
label: Recorded P6-01 replay · no new model or payment call
text: In this recorded split-refund example, the agent asks for sixty dollars while only forty remain available. A two-hundred-dollar cap is not enough. Counterfoil checks the return record and stops the request. The comparison on screen replays saved outcomes; it does not create a new payment.

title: A person decides exceptions
label: Illustrated review desk · not a live approval queue
text: A held request waits for the manager. The approval is bound to the exact call, expires, and can be used only once. The dashboard illustrates that review. The separate checkout flow can execute an approved refund on Braintree sandbox.

title: Measure harm, not just persuasion
label: October simulation · completed runs per condition
text: In the October simulation, harmful outcomes occurred in ninety-nine of two hundred seventy attack runs with no gate, one hundred with a cap, and zero with Counterfoil. Harm includes wrong money movement or another customer's data being read. These are measured runs, not a guarantee.

title: Keep experiments separate
label: November follow-ups · inspect each protocol and denominator
text: The newer experiments stay separate. The dashboard shows local attacks, hosted attacks, clean requests and repeated decisions with their own denominators. It preserves the stopped pilot and unknown outcome. Downloadable scored rows make each result inspectable.

title: What happens after a lost response?
label: 12 of 12 Braintree sandbox checks passed · 3 November 2026
text: We also tested approvals and locally injected payment failures against Braintree sandbox. All twelve cases passed. After reopening the ledger, retries did not create a second payment. Unknown outcomes still need reconciliation. The demo rejects old checkout IDs after restart; it does not resume those sessions automatically.

title: Try Counterfoil
label: counterfoil-demo.onrender.com  ·  counterfoil-dashboard.vercel.app
text: The complete offline suite passes five hundred thirty-three tests. Explore the recorded demo without an account, inspect the evidence dashboard, or try the separate sandbox checkout. Counterfoil asks a concrete question before money moves: does the merchant's record support this payment?
